title: Protocol for whole-brain immunostaining of the turquoise killifish after tissue clearing
protocol: Transfer fish to a 1.5 g/L tricaine solution.
Wait until the fish gills no longer move.
Touch the caudal fin to confirm that they do not respond.
Transfer whole fish into 30 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde in 1×PBS (pH7.4).
Incubate at 4°C from 6 to 24 h.
Cut the head between the gills and the pectoral fin.
Isolate the fish head and remove the lower jaw.
Flip the head upside-down.
Clear the palate muscle from the upper jaw with fine forceps.
Hold the spine to fix the head with fine tweezers.
Remove the eyes and gill covers.
Remove the eyes and gill cover.
Remove the head skin and muscle.
Cut the skull to reveal the brain.
Remove the upper skull to expose the brain.
Cut below the gills with scissors.
Remove the lower jaw and soft palate muscles.
Hold the spine tightly with forceps and cut out the eyes along the frontal skull.
Remove skin and muscle above the skull.
Cut from the infraorbital ring to the subopercle.
Carefully remove the frontal skull with fine forceps.
Remove the brain from the lower skull.
Put the isolated brain into 500 μL of the second fixation solution in the Binaree Tissue Clearing Starter’s kit.
Incubate without agitation for at least 6 h at 4°C.
Remove the fixation solution carefully with a pipette.
Add 200 μL of tissue clearing solution A to the fixed brain and gently invert the sample a few times, then discard the solution.
Add 500 μL of tissue clearing solution A and incubate the tube at 42°C for 3 days without shaking. Invert the tube gently a few times a day.
Remove tissue clearing solution A with a pipette, taking special care not to touch the brain.
Add 500 μL of washing solution and briefly wash out the tissue clearing solution A, then discard the solution.
Add 1 mL of washing solution and incubate the tube at 42°C for 8 hours.
Repeat the washing step twice. Invert the tube gently a few times per wash.
Remove the washing solution carefully with a pipette.
Add 200 μL of tissue clearing solution B to the sample and gently invert to mix.
Add 500 μL of tissue clearing solution B and incubate at 35°C for 2 days without shaking, inverting a few times daily.
Remove tissue clearing solution B carefully with a pipet, avoiding contact with the brain.
Add 500 μL of washing solution and briefly wash out the tissue clearing solution B.
Add 1 mL of washing solution and incubate at 35°C for 8 hours.
Repeat the washing step twice, inverting gently per wash.
Optional: Stop at this stage to store the brain up to a week at 4°C without further immunostaining.
Add DAPI solution (1 μL per 1 mL) for nuclear staining into the final washing solution and incubate at 35°C for 8 hours.
Remove the washing solution carefully with a pipet.
Add 200 μL of mounting and storage solution, agitating gently a few times.
Add 500 μL of mounting and storage solution.
Incubate the tube at 35°C for 12 hours.
Store the tube at 4°C in the dark for long-term storage up to 1 month before imaging.
Remove washing solution carefully with a pipet.
Gently wash the brain with 100 μL of staining solution.
Add 100 μL of staining solution containing antibody.
Incubate the brain with the anti-CLOCK antibody (1:200) at 4°C in the dark for 2 days without agitation.
Remove the antibody solution.
Add 1 mL of washing solution.
Incubate the tube at 35°C for 12 h without shaking and gently invert the tube from time to time during the incubation.
Repeat this three times.
Remove the washing solution carefully.
Gently wash the brain with 100 μL of staining solution.
Add 100 μL of staining solution containing a goat anti-rabbit IgG antibody conjugated with Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100).
Incubate the brain with the secondary antibody at 4°C in the dark for 2 days.
Remove the antibody solution and add 1 mL of washing solution.
Incubate the tube at 35°C for 12 h without shaking and gently invert the tube from time to time during the incubation.
Repeat this three times.
Remove the washing solution carefully with a pipette.
Add 200 μL of mounting and storage buffer.
Add 500 μL of mounting and storage buffer.
Incubate the sample at 35°C for 12 hours without shaking.
Gently invert the tube from time to time during the incubation.
Check the fluorescence briefly using a fluorescence microscope.
Store the tube at 4°C in the dark until imaging.
Completely melt 2% low melting temperature agarose in PBS.
Cool down the 2% agarose solution to around 60°C.
Select a proper-size capillary for the prepared brain.
Pour 3 mL of agarose into a Petri dish.
Place the brain onto the Petri dish in the agarose after brief washing with PBS.
Transfer the brain into the agarose on the Petri dish and gently rotate the dish to cover the brain with the agarose.
Fill a capillary halfway with agarose, taking care to avoid bubbles.
Place the capillary at the posterior brain and suck the brain into the capillary using a plunger.
Make sure the brain is placed 0.5–1 cm from the tip of the capillary and that there are no air bubbles.
Wait until the agarose solidifies.
Place the sample chamber onto the microscope.
Fill the chamber with PBS or mounting and storage buffer.
Place a capillary tube onto the sample holder.
Place the brain embedded in agarose in front of the objective lens by pushing the plunger.
Rotate the embedded brain so that the dorsal or ventral part of the brain is facing the objective lens.
Choose a filter set with the proper excitation and emission.
Check the fluorescence intensity and focus.
Execute a tile imaging experiment covering the whole brain.
Define the Z-depth, capturing the region from the cerebellum to the pituitary.
Define the corner at the top left.
Define the corner at the bottom right.
Save this corner-defined file as file_name.mlv in ZEN 2014 SP1.
Read file_name.mlv from Lightsheet Z.1 Tile Scan.
Create a pseudo tile array (usually with a 10% overlap between tiles).
Save this file as file_name2.mlv.
If the brain is too thick, flip the brain vertically and repeat steps from 11c to 11f.
Use the same parameters for imaging including gain, exposure time, and laser intensity when comparing protein expression between two brains.
Perform test trials to check general fluorescence intensity.
Adjust imaging parameters on a sample with strong fluorescence intensity.
Convert file_name.czi files generated using the same imaging conditions into Imaris files (file_name.ims) using Imaris File Converter.
Read files in Imaris Sticher and automatically array tiled raw images.
Adjust edges of raw images and run stitching.
Check merged image and individual images using slide sections.
Adjust minimum and maximum intensity, gamma, and opacity in each channel.
Apply the same image display parameters to other brains and export images.
Crop regions of interest from whole brain images or single tile images.
Read files in Zen (file_name.czi) or Imaris (file_name.ims).
Adjust image display using the same parameters for image display.
Export images.
